dedupe_keys.name: washington state low earth orbit satellite broadband feasibility report to the legislature 2023

description: This case study is the Washington State Broadband Office's report to the Legislature, of December 2023, on whether low Earth orbit satellite service can help reach universal broadband in the state. The Department of Commerce prepared it under Chapter 474, Laws of 2023 (SB 5200, section 1037), to guide how the federal Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) programme is spent. It reviews LEO technology, examples of its use in Washington, and costs per broadband serviceable location by county, and finds that LEO can be deployed quickly and flexibly where terrestrial broadband is costly because of low density and hard terrain, and can support network resilience in emergencies. Because BEAD treats LEO as an unreliable technology, the report expects its role in the state plan to be limited to special high-cost cases. Coverage is Washington State. Format and access: a 26-page PDF on the Legislature's reports site. Licence: not stated; a public government report; free. Caveats: a policy assessment, not a technical performance test, and the BEAD rules may change. It supports capacity planning of rural telecom infrastructure. A related catalogue record is the NewSpace Index of satellite constellations.
